items.text: Praying for extra strength and a full recovery for @SteveScalise as he begins treatment. We all know he’s a fighter and will overcome this challenge.

Congress did not give the ATF the authority to criminalize the exercise of Second Amendment rights.
 
The amicus brief I signed onto opposes the ATF’s arm brace rule and its outrageous overreach.

North Carolinians are already suffering from high inflation and interest rates. I joined @RepGregMurphy to stop the excessive increase in homeowner insurance rates that would only worsen the cost-of-living crisis constituents are already facing. #ncpol

While protesters have a right to exercise their freedom of speech, they don’t have the right to block our highways and roads.

Read about the Safe and Open Streets Act that I helped introduce in light of radical acts of protests we’ve seen across our country: https://t.co/FludsBHPbO
Don’t forget to set your clocks one hour ahead for Daylight Saving Time before you go to sleep tonight! https://t.co/uunzhw1xvu

Thank you to the @60PlusAssoc for presenting me with the Guardian of Seniors’ Rights Award for supporting policies to eliminate the death tax and protect Social Security and Medicare for our seniors. As the representative for #NC11, I’ll continue to be a voice for seniors across our mountains.

On National Former Prisoner of War Recognition Day, we honor U.S. service members who have sacrificed their rights and suffered unimaginable treatment under the hand of their captors to defend the freedom of their fellow Americans.

This day reminds us of the high cost of freedom, and our nation is eternally grateful for the service and sacrifice of all former prisoners of war.
It’s National Nurses Week, a time to celebrate and show appreciation for #NC11 nurses who care and advocate for patients across our mountains. https://t.co/WjuiAvOYKw

The U.S. is seeing a surge in hospital mergers, resulting in increased federal health spending and higher patient costs, and yet patients are experiencing lower quality of care.

We’ve seen this right here in our mountains and as a member of @housebudgetGOP  and @HouseAppropsGOP, it’s my mission to promote policies and funding that disincentive consolidation and promote greater choice, more affordable access and better quality of care for the citizens of #NC11 and beyond.
https://t.co/AbVWqSiZ2O

This week, @HouseGOP advanced nearly three dozen bills to counter the Chinese Communist Party’s rising threat, including:

✅ Maintaining U.S. independence from the World Health Organization in pandemic policy-making
✅ Keeping the CCP out of our colleges
✅ Protecting our national and food security from foreign land grabs

Grant news for #NC11: Two Appalachian Regional Commission grants are coming to Western North Carolina to increase workforce participation.

Jackson County's HIGHTS will receive $18,000 to expand the behavioral health workforce in WNC, and @LandofSkyRC will receive nearly $500,000 for their partnership with substance use treatment courts to provide workforce training to recovering addicts.

It’s encouraging to see these resources coming to our district to better our community.

#NC11: Hurricane Helene update #8 includes information on resources for farmers, prescription access for veterans and the uninsured, new federal nutrition program flexibilities and resources for how to vote in a post-Hurricane Helene environment.
https://t.co/DO3rgxkNNh

The Dept. of Health & Human Sevices’ Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response has approximately 240 personnel deployed to support public health and medical needs in WNC post-Hurricane Helene. We are thankful for them stepping in to serve our communities at Mission Hospital and Blue Ridge Regional Hospital.

The Mission Health/A-B Tech Conference Center is serving as a Red Cross shelter for Buncombe County. Some of the residents include veterans who had to relocate after the Veterans Restoration Quarters was flooded. Medical staff and volunteers from Arkansas to Illinois are there to join the effort to help Western North Carolinians through recovery after Hurricane Helene.

#NC11: Hurricane Helene update #10 includes details on where to find critical health care services including orthopedic care, dialysis treatments, and oxygen tanks, and an updated timeline on power restoration for folks in the hardest-hit areas.
https://t.co/GUTYBMm7Sf

#NC11: Hurricane Helene update #12 includes best practices for navigating storm debris removal, mental health resources, and updates on where to find a hot meal, progress on the I-40 westbound repair process, and steps being taken by the Asheville VA to shore up their water source.
https://t.co/GVvK5cZUEA

WNC is grateful for the health care professionals and the National Disaster Medical System team who are stepping in and working tirelessly to provide care for patients at Blue Ridge Regional Hospital post-Hurricane Helene. https://t.co/w0joTie60U

#NC11: Hurricane Helene recovery update #23 includes information on early voting sites that were closed due to Helene, the end of a “do not travel” advisory in Western NC and the number of wastewater treatment centers operating normally across our mountains.
https://t.co/VNbdkNxBmV

Today is Election Day and voting is an opportunity to exercise your greatest liberty and make your voice is heard.

Due to hurricane damage, some voting sites have changed in Western North Carolina. If you’re unsure where your Election Day polling place is located, you can visit this link and put in your address: https://t.co/toMszlNQ8m 

Please note that voting on Election Day is not the same as early voting, and you must go to your assigned polling place.

For the love of democracy, get out and vote.

On Veterans Day, the Charles George VA Medical Center and many communities across our mountains are honoring those who served our nation in the armed forces. Freedom isn’t free, and we are forever grateful to America’s heroes for their courage and sacrifice. https://t.co/SxWSvdQrkp

#NC11: Hurricane Helene recovery update #31 includes information on the FEMA assistance deadlines, reopening of the Yancey County DMV, Blue Ridge Health locations and hours, where you can pick up mail from your PO Box in Barnardsville, a new Disaster Recovery Center in Macon County, and a change in location for the Buncombe County Disaster Recovery Center.
https://t.co/UK1A6Tj3nL

Saint Bernard Parish is partnering with @HAC_Housing, AT&T and Farmers Insurance to host a Regional Recovery Acceleration Week in #NC11 for elected officials, foundations leaders and recovery NGOs to help facilitate a prompt, efficient and predictable recovery in the aftermath of Hurricane Helene.
 
To sign up for Regional Recovery Acceleration Week, visit https://t.co/mo52dzGODw contact mgonzalez@sbpusa.org.

📢 Attention Macon and Swain County citizens: The Disaster Recovery Centers at the following locations will be closing as of 2:00 p.m. on Saturday, December 14.
- Macon County Public Health Center, 1830 Lakeside Dr., Franklin, NC
- Swain County Technology and Training Center, 45 East Ridge Dr., Bryson City, NC

To find the remaining open locations, visit https://t.co/1v9NNtasm1. If you need assistance with FEMA, call my office at 223-FIX-FEMA.

As the branch of government with the power of the purse, we’ve let spending get out of control.

I’m working to fix how Washington works and end the careless spending that’s destroying the economic health of our nation.
https://t.co/ri2Z3kOW5H

📢 Henderson County residents: If you’ve been affected by Hurricane Helene and don’t have debris removal insurance, you can apply to have qualified disaster debris removed from your property at no cost through the Private Property Debris Removal Program.
 
For more information, visit https://t.co/rPa9NoEz1c.
